title: to_ipv6 preserves scope_id so routing keys split
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py to_ipv6() returns IPv6Address as-is, including scope_id. make_link_local() and link_local_from_pubkey() now attach zone_id. Python treats these as unequal:

IPv6Address('fe80::1%eth0') != IPv6Address('fe80::1')

Both are used as OrderedDict keys in RouteCache, GradientTable, and RPL. Insert via a zoned link-local, lookup from a wire-derived unzoned address, miss.

## Why it matters

Zones are never on the wire (.packed omits them). After the zone_id work, the same 128-bit LCI/link-local can exist in zoned and unzoned form. Silent route miss, not an error.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:30-47 to_ipv6, 125-145 make_link_local
python/src/lichen/loadng/cache.py:73 _entries keyed by IPv6Address
python/src/lichen/gradient.py:118 same
design: Zone is local interface metadata (make_link_local docstring). Routing tables must key on the 128-bit address. Either strip scope in to_ipv6, or add an explicit packed-key helper and switch loadng/gradient/rpl to it. Do not drop zone from make_link_local return values used for local send.
acceptance_criteria: A zoned and unzoned form of the same 128-bit address must compare equal as routing keys, or to_ipv6/docs must stop being used as a dict key without packing. Add a test that lookup(fe80::1) finds an entry inserted as fe80::1%lci0 (or the chosen canonical form). Wire packed bytes still round-trip.
close_reason: routing_key canonicalizes on packed 128-bit bytes so fe80::1 and fe80::1%zone share RouteCache/GradientTable/RPL keys; to_ipv6 still preserves scope_id for local send; independent packed-oracle tests pass
